author: Makoto Shinkai
description:
Told in three interconnected segments, Takaki tells the story of his life as cruel winters, cold technology, and finally, adult obligations and responsibility converge to test the delicate petals of love.
Director Makoto Shinkai

There is a question whispered at the start of our story:
How fast do cherry blossoms fall?

The answer: about five centimeters per second.

Just like the drifting petals, human hearts, too, can fall… softly, slowly, and sometimes apart.

This is the story of Takaki Tōno — a boy, a teenager, a man — whose life unfolds in three chapters.
A story of love, distance, and the gentle ache of time.

This miracle would grow into a legend — of beauty, love, sorrow, and fate.
This is the story of the girl from the moon… The Tale of the Princess Kaguya.

video_title: Sweet Porridge   Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm
description:
Sweet Porridge   Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm

Sweet Porridge - Fairy Tale by the Brothers Grimm


There was a poor but good little girl who lived alone with her mother, and they no longer had anything to eat. So the child went into the forest, and there an aged woman met her who was aware of her sorrow, and presented her with a little pot, which when she said, „Cook, little pot, cook,“ would cook good, sweet porridge, and when she said, „Stop, little pot,“ it ceased to cook.

The girl took the pot home to her mother, and now they were freed from their poverty and hunger, and ate sweet porridge as often as they chose. Once on a time when the girl had gone out, her mother said, „Cook, little pot, cook.“ And it did cook and she ate till she was satisfied, and then she wanted the pot to stop cooking, but did not know the word.


So it went on cooking and the porridge rose over the edge, and still it cooked on until the kitchen and whole house were full, and then the next house, and then the whole street, just as if it wanted to satisfy the hunger of the whole world, and there was the greatest distress, but no one knew how to stop it.

At last when only one single house remained, the child came home and just said, „Stop, little pot,“ and it stopped and gave up cooking, and whosoever wished to return to the town had to eat his way back.

description:
Medusa is one of the most haunting and fascinating figures in Greek mythology 🐍.
Her story is a mix of beauty, tragedy, and monstrous transformation.
🧬 Origins and Family
Medusa was one of the three Gorgon sisters—alongside Stheno and Euryale.
Unlike her immortal siblings, Medusa was mortal, which made her vulnerable to death.
She was the daughter of Phorcys and Ceto, primordial sea gods.
💔 The Curse of Athena
Medusa was originally a beautiful maiden, admired for her stunning hair.
According to myth, she was either boastful about her beauty or violated by Poseidon in Athena’s temple.
Enraged, Athena transformed her into a monster with snakes for hair and a gaze that turned people to stone.
⚔️ Perseus and the Slaying
The hero Perseus was sent on a quest to slay Medusa.
With help from Athena and Hermes, he used a bronze shield to view her reflection and avoid her deadly gaze.
He beheaded Medusa while she slept, and from her blood sprang Pegasus (the winged horse) and Chrysaor, her children by Poseidon.
🛡️ Legacy and Symbolism
Perseus gave Medusa’s head to Athena, who placed it on her shield (the Aegis) as a protective emblem.
Her image became a symbol of protection and was used on armor and buildings to ward off evil.
Medusa’s myth has been reinterpreted over time—some see her as a tragic victim, others as a symbol of feminine rage and power.

author: Makoto Shinkai
description:
Your Name is Japanese anime which Directed by Makoto Shinkai, the animation studio behind the movie Your Name is responsible for some of the most beautiful animated films ever made.
And Your Name is no exception. The movie follows two teenagers who share a profound, magical connection despite never having met before.
Takki Takachi Bana, a teenage boy from Tokyo, and Mizuhami Amemiya, a teenage girl who lives with her grandmother and little sister in the countryside, find themselves inexplicably drawn to each other.
Their connection is so strong that they begin to feel emotions and sensations that they have never felt before.
And they soon discover that they are swapping bodies whenever they fall asleep.
At first, they try to make the best of the situation and enjoy the newfound experiences that come with being in someone else 's body.
However, as time goes on, they begin to feel the downsides of not being able to control their own bodies
and the emotional toll it takes on them and those around them.
They make a pact to meet in person for the first time and try to sort things out.
But when they do meet, things don't exactly go according to plan.
The boy finds the girl's body and takes it back to his home in Tokyo, intending to return it to her the next day.
However, the girl's little sister gets sick and the boy ends up taking care of her instead.
In the meantime, the girl's grandmother becomes suspicious of the boy's presence in the house and confronts him.
She threatens to call the police if he doesn't leave, so the boy is forced to escape.
He runs into a convenience store and bumps into a friend of his who invites him to go see a fireworks festival with some other friends.
The boy accepts and spends the night with his friends, drinking, partying and letting loose.
Meanwhile, the girl wakes up in her own body again and is relieved to be reunited with her little sister.
The next morning, she finds a mysterious blue umbrella on the ground, which turns out to be a memento from the boy.
She keeps the umbrella and returns to Tokyo to find the boy and give him back his body.
But when she gets there, she finds that he has disappeared.
All she has to show for her adventure is a blue umbrella and a handful of memories.
Your Name is a beautifully animated film with a touching story and memorable characters.
It's a must-watch for fans of romance and body swap movies.
So if you haven't seen it yet, I highly recommend checking it out.

description:
Grave of the Fireflies.
It's no secret that Japan was one of the most heavily bombed countries during World War II.
And in 1945, near the end of the war, an American B29 Super Fortress made a low altitude pass over the Japanese city of Kobe.
Its target, a factory complex that produced 80 percent of Japan's munitions. But the plane's bombardier made a mistake.
He dropped his payload early, killing hundreds of innocent civilians.
Among the dead were two children, a brother and sister who had been playing near their home when the bombs fell.
Their story is this anime's only reason for existing, though it's been retold countless times before.
It follows Seita and his little sister, who wake up in the hospital with no memory of the attack.
They're eventually discharged and they set out to find their mother, who they believe is still alive.
But their journey is fraught with danger. Food and supplies are scarce and the siblings must brave the elements and the hostility of strangers just to stay alive.
Along the way, they meet a handful of quirky characters, including an old woman who takes them in and a group of children who befriend them.
But the adults in this world are mostly uncaring and the children are forced to fend for themselves.
The animation is gorgeous, but the story is painfully slow.
For the first 20 minutes, not a single word is spoken.
The film 's first few scenes are so effective that it 's hard to imagine how the story could possibly go anywhere from there.
So if you're expecting Grave of the Fireflies to be a sweeping epic, you'll probably be disappointed.
If, however, you're in the mood for a character study, this movie is perfect.
We get to see how far a young boy will go to protect his sister and how far a little girl will go to protect her brother.
Their relationship is the heart and soul of this movie.
And while it might not have the action and excitement of other wartime movies, it's all the better for it.
This is a quiet, character-driven drama that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

author: Andrew Lang
description:
Goldilocks and the Three Bears,
Based on the Charming version by the Victorian writer Andrew Lang.

Once upon a time there were three bears, who lived together in a house of their own in a wood. One of them was a little, small wee bear; one was a middle-sized bear, and the other was a great, huge bear.

One day, after they had made porridge for their breakfast, they walked out into the wood while the porridge was cooling. And while they were walking, a little girl came into the house. This little girl had golden curls that tumbled down her back to her waist, and everyone called her by Goldilocks.

Goldilocks went inside. First she tasted the porridge of the great, huge bear, and that was far too hot for her. And then she tasted the porridge of the middle bear, and that was too cold for her. And then she went to the porridge of the little, small wee bear, and tasted that. And that was neither too hot nor too cold, but just right; and she liked it so well, that she ate it all up.

Then Goldilocks went upstairs into the bed chamber and first she lay down upon the bed of the great, huge bear, and then she lay down upon the bed of the middle bear and finally she lay down upon the bed of the little, small wee bear, and that was just right. So she covered herself up comfortably, and lay there until she fell fast asleep.

By this time, the three bears thought their porridge would be cool enough, so they came home to breakfast.

“SOMEBODY HAS BEEN AT MY PORRIDGE!” said the great huge bear, in his great huge voice.

“Somebody has been at my porridge!” said the middle bear, in his middle voice.

Then the little, small wee bear looked at his, and there was the spoon in the porridge pot, but the porridge was all gone.

“Somebody has been at my porridge, and has eaten it all up!” said the little, small wee bear, in his little, small wee voice.

Then the three bears went upstairs into their bedroom.

“SOMEBODY HAS BEEN LYING IN MY BED!” said the great, huge bear, in his great, rough, gruff voice.

“Somebody has been lying in my bed!” said the middle bear, in his middle voice.

And when the little, small, wee bear came to look at his bed, upon the pillow there was a pool of golden curls, and the angelic face of a little girl snoring away, fast asleep.

“Somebody has been lying in my bed, and here she is!” Said the little, small wee bear, in his little, small wee voice.

Goldilocks jumped off the bed and ran downstairs, out of the door and down the garden path. She ran and she ran until she reached the house of her grandmama. When she told her grandmama about the house of the three bears who lived in the wood, her granny said: “My my, what a wild imagination you have, child!”

description:
Rapunzel
Rapunzel was a princess kidnapped by a witch when she was a kid for her magical hair. Rapunzel did not know that she was kidnapped by the witch pretending to be her mother, and she wanted her for her magical hair. Every day the witch combed Rapunzel's long beautiful hair  so that by touching her hair, she could look younger than her real age. Witch every time, Witch lies to Rapunzel that the outside world is not good for her, and she should always sit in their castle for their safety.
Slowly, Rapunzel discovered the outside world with the help of a stranger she met at her castle and faced many obstacles in the outside world and discovered that the witch was not her birth mother; she kidnapped her. Rapunzel learnt that she had magical long hair, for which the witch wanted her. Ultimately, she bravely fought the witch and reunited with her birth parents.

video_title: Mid Autumn Festival or the Moon Festival
description:
The Mid Autumn Festival or the Moon Festival is a traditional Chinese holiday celebrated every year on the 15th day of the 8th month on the Chinese calendar.
This year it falls on September. It's a time for family reunions, just like Thanksgiving here in the States, but with a lunar twist.
The holiday is all about appreciating the beauty of the moon and giving thanks to the moon goddess Chang' e.
According to legend, Chang' e was an ordinary woman who was chosen to become the moon goddess after she accidentally drank an elixir that was meant for her husband, the Jade Emperor.
After she ascended to the moon, she was lonely and each year on this day, her husband would visit her and they would enjoy the reunion until, you know, he kicked her to the curb for good.
So, you know, the Jade Emperor, he's not really the nice guy you want to be stuck at home with.
Anyway, people celebrate the holiday by getting together with their families and eating mooncakes.
Mooncakes are delicious pastries filled with sweet or savory ingredients and they come in all shapes and sizes, just like the moon, which is said to be at its fullest and brightest on this night.
The round shape of the mooncakes symbolize the full moon and the reunion of families.
The most popular flavor is probably the lotus seed paste, but there's also bean, red bean, coconut, egg yolk, green tea and even durian.
You can also get really fancy ones like this five thousand dollar gold one that's actually edible. No joke.
Another fun thing about the holiday is the lantern riddles.
During the Lantern Festival, which takes place the day after the Moon Festival, people will set up elaborate lanterns
and then take turns trying to guess the riddles that are written on them.
Whoever guesses correctly gets to keep the lantern.
So if you're in China for this holiday, be sure to try some mooncakes and maybe even do a little lantern riddle guessing.
And if you can't be in China, then just stay up late and appreciate the moon from wherever you are.
Because even though we might be miles away from our loved ones, we can still come together and appreciate the beauty of the natural world.
Just don't stare too long at your phone. Put it down, look up and take in the view.
After all, that's what the moon goddess Chang'e would want us to do.
Thanks for watching and I'll see you next time.

description:
Once upon a time in a spooky old house on a dark and stormy night, there lived a kind witch named Hazel.
She brewed magical potions and cast delightful spells, spreading joy throughout the neighborhood.
But alas, her sister, the dreadful Griselda, practiced wicked witchcraft and longed to rule the town with an iron fist.
Now, despite their differences, they shared one thing in common, a deep love for cats.
And when a lost kitten meowed pitifully on their doorstep, Hazel took it in without hesitation.
But Griselda, with her heart as cold as a witch's cauldron, flung the poor creature out into the storm.
"A witch's house is no place for a stray," she cackled.
"Quick, get out of here before I turn you into a toad."
However, something remarkable happened.
Instead of cowering in fear, the kitten stood its ground, arched its back and let out a mighty roar that shook the very foundations of the house.
Startled by this unexpected display of bravery, Griselda retreated into her room, leaving Hazel to care for the kitten.
As the days passed, the kitten grew stronger and more courageous, and Hazel couldn't help but feel a sense of pride.
She named him Midnight and taught him how to fish for compliments with a magic wand and yarn ball.
Together, they explored the enchanting Whispering Woods, where trees gossiped secrets and flowers bloomed in every color imaginable.
Meanwhile, Griselda seethed with envy, watching from afar as Hazel and Midnight became the talk of the town.
"That wretched cat has brought nothing but chaos to my peaceful home," she grumbled.
"I must do something drastic before my cauldron bubbles over with rage."
And so the wicked witch concocted a wicked plan.
She transformed herself into a beautiful white dove and flew to the village, where she cast a spell on the baker, causing him to fall madly in love with the first person he laid eyes on, which, ugh, just happened to be Griselda.
Then she repeated the process with the cobbler, the tailor and every eligible bachelor in town until she had an entire army of lovestruck men at her command.
With their help, she marched on Hazel's house, determined to put an end to her sister's happiness once and for all.
But little did she know that Midnight had overheard her plans and had already alerted his fairy godmother, the great and powerful Luna.
As Griselda's goons approached the house, Luna swooped down from the sky, transforming Midnight into a magnificent lion with a flick of her magic wand.
Startled by the sudden appearance of a real life Disney character, the men froze in their tracks.
Then, with a deafening roar, the lion pounced, sending them running for their lives.
Griselda, however, was not so easily defeated. She raised her hands and unleashed a torrent of dark magic, but Luna was unfazed.
With a wave of her wand, she banished Griselda's spells and sent her tumbling into her own cauldron.
"It's over, Griselda," Luna boomed. "Your reign of terror ends today."
But before she could finish the job, a tiny meow interrupted her.
Startled, Luna turned and saw Hazel standing before her, holding a small, familiar looking kitten in her arms.
"Please, Great Luna," Hazel pleaded. "My sister may be misguided, but she's still my family.
I beg you, spare her life and turn her into a cat instead."
Touched by Hazel's compassion, Luna agreed. And with a wave of her magic wand, Griselda was transformed into a fluffy grey tabby cat.
As the townspeople looked on, Hazel and Griselda embraced, realizing that love and kindness were far more powerful than any curse or spell.
They lived happily ever after, or at least until next week's episode.

video_title: Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain
description:
Even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain.
That's what this saying in Japanese means. And it's a great life lesson for us all to remember.
Imagine a young man who wants to be the strongest, most successful businessman in the world.
He sets this big goal for himself. And every day he thinks about how far he is from actually achieving that goal. He feels so little and so powerless.
So he just gives up and figures he'll never accomplish anything because he's not special.
Now imagine another man who also wants to be the strongest businessman in the world. But every day he just does a little bit of reading.
He learns one new thing and practices that one new thing for the rest of the day.
He does this for a week and then goes back to work the next week and applies what he learned that week.
And he does this consistently until one day he becomes the most successful businessman in the world.
It's the same exact goal, but why did only one of them achieve it?
It's because of this saying, Chiri mo tsumoreba yama to naru, even dust, when piled up, will become a mountain.
No matter how small your efforts are, if you do them consistently over a long period of time, they will add up and become significant.
We often think we need to do something big to change our lives, but that's just not true. We can change our lives with small consistent efforts.
The secret to success in anything is to break it down into smaller actions.
For example, if you want to be the best at basketball, you can break it down into smaller actions like shooting 10 free throws every day or running 1 mile every day.
Once you have these small goals, it's much easier to achieve them and you'll see progress much faster.
And here's the beautiful thing about this quote. It doesn't matter what you do, only that you do it consistently.
The type of action doesn't matter as much as the consistency of the action.
You could be watering other people's plants and it would still apply.
As long as you're consistent, your efforts will eventually turn into a mountain, even if that mountain isn't exactly what you had envisioned.
So my question for you is, what small effort can you do today that will make a big difference in your life tomorrow? What small habits can you start building?
And I want you to really think about this because it's a serious question.
If you can identify those small actions, then you're one step closer to changing your life.
If you liked this video, please leave a like and subscribe.
It really helps me out. Thanks for watching and I'll see you next time.
